cards.q: What is SSL VPN and what are its two flavors?
cards.a: SSL VPN gives remote users secure access through a web browser or AnyConnect client using TLS/HTTPS on port 443, with no pre-installed IPsec client. The two flavors are clientless (portal to internal apps) and AnyConnect full-tunnel.
SSL VPN rides TLS over TCP 443, which passes through most firewalls and NAT, making it the main advantage over IPsec for remote access.

cards.q: What is the difference between clientless and AnyConnect SSL VPN modes?
cards.a: Clientless mode is a browser-based portal that provides access to internal apps with zero install; AnyConnect mode installs a full VPN tunnel providing complete network access.

cards.q: What is the difference between TLS and DTLS in an AnyConnect full-tunnel VPN?
cards.a: TLS (TCP 443) is the primary transport; DTLS (UDP 443) is the optimized transport that reduces latency for real-time applications.

cards.q: What security layers does SSL VPN use for authentication and posture?
cards.a: User authentication uses LDAP/RADIUS/AAA; MFA uses a token or certificate; posture uses endpoint checking via AnyConnect; and group policy defines split-tunnel or full-tunnel behavior.

cards.q: What is the comparison between SSL VPN and IPsec remote access?
cards.a: SSL VPN uses a browser or AnyConnect client and port 443 that works anywhere, offers fine-grained app access and moderate corporate control with low setup friction; IPsec RA requires an IPsec client and ports 500/4500 that are often blocked, offers full-tunnel, strong control, but higher setup friction. SSL VPN wins on reachability while IPsec wins on raw control.

cards.q: What are typical headend platforms for SSL VPN?
cards.a: Cisco ASA/ASAv or ISR hosts the SSL VPN service; AnyConnect is licensed per user and group-policies define access. ISR uses the webvpn gateway syntax, while ASA uses ASDM/ASA syntax.

cards.q: Which commands verify SSL VPN sessions?
cards.a: show vpn-sessiondb anyconnect, show vpn-sessiondb svc, show webvpn, and show crypto ikev2 sa.

cards.q: The SSL VPN portal is unreachable; what is a likely cause?
cards.a: Port 443 is blocked by an ACL on the path; check the ACL permitting TCP 443 to the headend.

cards.q: A remote user has no full tunnel even though the SSL VPN authenticates; what should you check?
cards.a: The split-tunnel versus full-tunnel policy is set by the group-policy; check that the group-policy is not set to split-tunnel limiting the networks.

cards.q: Why does SSL VPN beat IPsec for per-user reachability through NAT and firewalls?
cards.a: SSL VPN uses TCP 443 (TLS), which passes through nearly all NAT and firewalls, whereas IPsec uses ports 500/4500 that are often blocked, so SSL VPN provides better per-user reachability.

cards.q: What is the SSL VPN quick-review summary?
cards.a: SSL VPN uses TLS on 443, has clientless and AnyConnect modes, full tunnel via AnyConnect, fast path via DTLS 443, browser or client, AAA/MFA/cert auth, is NAT friendly, and is compared with IPsec remote access.
